walkthroughs.body_html:
Further Mechanics — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Further Mechanics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Further Mechanics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In any collision within an isolated system, which quantity is always conserved?
options: Momentum
Kinetic energy
The velocity of each object
The speed of each object

mcqs.q: An object moves in a circle at constant speed. Its acceleration is:
options: Directed along its velocity.
Directed away from the centre.
Directed towards the centre of the circle.
Zero, because the speed is constant.
Force divided by time
Mass times acceleration squared
The change in momentum
The change in kinetic energy

mcqs.q: A 2 kg trolley moving at 3 m/s collides with and sticks to a stationary 1 kg trolley. Their combined speed is:
options: 3 m/s
6 m/s
2 m/s

mcqs.q: A car turns a corner at constant speed. Is it accelerating?
options: Gravity reverses direction at high speed.
Only if the road is banked.
No — constant speed means zero acceleration.
Yes — its velocity changes direction, so it has a centripetal acceleration.

mcqs.q: What 'centrifugal force' flings you outwards on a roundabout?
options: No real outward force acts — you feel your own inertia while a centripetal force pulls you towards the centre.
A real outward centrifugal force acts on you.
Only if the road is banked.
Gravity reverses direction at high speed.

mcqs.q: Is momentum lost when two cars crumple together in a crash?
options: Yes — momentum is destroyed by friction and crumpling.
No — kinetic energy is conserved instead.
No — total momentum is conserved; kinetic energy is transferred to deformation, sound and heat.
Gravity reverses direction at high speed.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Momentum”?
options: A collision in which momentum is conserved but some kinetic energy is transferred to other forms.
The change in momentum of an object, equal to force multiplied by the time for which it acts: FΔt = Δp.
The acceleration of an object in circular motion, directed towards the centre: a = v²/r.
The product of mass and velocity, p = mv; a vector quantity measured in kg m/s.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Inelastic collision”?
options: A collision in which both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved.
The acceleration of an object in circular motion, directed towards the centre: a = v²/r.
A collision in which momentum is conserved but some kinetic energy is transferred to other forms.
The total momentum of an isolated system is unchanged in any collision or explosion.
